messages.subject: Predictions in alternative scenarios
parts:
Hi all,

I am fitting a model using the following formula:

formula <- outbreaks ~  duck + chicken + otherpoultry + 
  f(idareau, model = "besag", graph = adj_inla) +
  f(idareav, model = "iid")

result <- inla(formula, family = "binomial", data = data_inla, Ntrials = susceptibles,
                           control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link=1),
                           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, return.marginals.predictor = TRUE, return.marginals = TRUE, config=TRUE))

and I get predictions for some areas with NAs. However, I would also like to obtain predictions in alternative scenarios, where the number of ducks is reduced and the number of susceptibles is also reduced. Is there a way to reuse the same model coefficients, adjacency matrix and random effects and re-run the model to update the predictions in these alternative scenarios? 

I know I could make a big dataframe with both the actual data in the data in the alternative scenarios with NAs, replicate the adjacency matrix, and just fit the model and run the predictions for everything in one go but that seems somewhat artificial to me, so I was wondering if there is a better way to do it.  

Thank you in advance!
Clara Delecroix

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Predictions in alternative scenarios
parts:
the easy way out, is just to append your alternative scenarios to the data, with
NA response.

like

dat=data.frame(y=1:2, x=2:3)
new = data.frame(y=c(NA,NA), x=c(20,30))

data = rbind(dat,new)
